claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex.

Let me ask a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you.

Now, could you tell me about your residency status? Are you currently living in the UK, and do you have the right to live in the UK (for example, are you a UK citizen, have settled status, or have another immigration status that allows you to live here)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. I'm a UK citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

One more question: Is Alex in full-time education or training, and is he currently in any form of local authority care, or has he been in hospital for an extended period?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Well, he's 8, so he's at primary school - just normal school for his age. 

Actually, he was in local authority care recently, but it was just for a short time - maybe a couple of months or so.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. It's helpful to know about Alex's recent time in local authority care.

Could you clarify: has Alex now returned to living with you, or is he still in local authority care? And if he has returned, approximately how long ago did he come back home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's back home with me now. It's been finished for a bit - he came back a few weeks ago.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great to hear that Alex is back home with you.

Just one more question about his time in care: while Alex was in local authority care, was it for more than 8 weeks continuously, or was it less than 8 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was less than 8 weeks - just under, really.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on what you've told me:

- You are a UK citizen living in the UK
- Alex is 8 years old and lives with you
- He is in full-time education (primary school) as expected for his age
- He was in local authority care for less than 8 weeks and has now returned home

This is good news! Let me provide you with my assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of my assessment:

**For Alex (age 8):** ✅ Eligible

- ✅ He is under 16 years old
- ✅ He lives with you, meaning you're responsible for him
- ✅ You are a UK citizen living in the UK
- ✅ Although Alex was recently in local authority care, it was for less than 8 weeks, which is below the threshold that would affect your Child Benefit entitlement

The fact that Alex was briefly in care doesn't impact your eligibility since it was under 8 weeks and he has now returned home to live with you.

If you haven't already, you can apply for Child Benefit through the official government channels. Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
